text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.75. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.75.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.75 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 45 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working through the payoff structure of this token game—each kept token nets me 1 point but costs others 0.75 each, while group account tokens pay out 0.75 to me without that spillover penalty, so I'm trying to pin down how the group contributions actually get distributed.

So individually, private contribution still dominates (1 vs 0.75 per token), but full cooperation leaves everyone far better off than mutual defection—each member nets 60 by pooling everything versus -25 by keeping it all private. Given this is a repeated 10-round game, I think starting cooperatively by contributing the full 20 makes sense as a signal, and I'll watch how the group responds.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working through the public goods game payoff structure: keeping a token privately nets +1 self and -0.75 to each other member, while contributing to the group account gives everyone a 0.75 share. I'm calculating the social optimum where everyone contributes fully, since each token invested generates 0.75 returns to all four members collectively.

Working through the math: if everyone defects fully, each person nets 20 points, but if everyone cooperates fully, each nets 60 points—cooperation is far better collectively. Since this is repeated and signaling matters, I'll contribute all 20 tokens to the group in this first round to encourage mutual cooperation and see how the total plays out.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This looks like a public goods game with a negative externality on private holdings. I'm working out each member's payoff: private tokens earn 1 point each but cost other members 0.75 points per token, while group contributions redistribute 0.75 points to everyone.

I'm trying to figure out whether the formula means each group token pays the contributor 0.75 points directly, or whether contributions sum into a shared pool that's then split evenly among all members — this distinction matters a lot for calculating the dominant strategy and total welfare effects of shifting a token from the group account to the private account.

Being exploited costs relatively little (15 vs 20) while mutual cooperation pays much more (60 vs 20), so starting with a strong contribution seems worth the risk. I'll open with a contribution of 20 to signal cooperative intent, then adjust in later rounds based on the group's total.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This looks like a public goods game with a negative externality on private holdings. I'm working out that my payoff equals the endowment plus my own private tokens, minus 0.75 for each token others keep privately, plus my share of the group total.

Group tokens only pay 0.75 to the contributor and don't affect anyone else's points, while private tokens pay 1 to me but cost each other member 0.75. So individually, keeping tokens private (1 point) dominates contributing to the group (0.75 points) — but socially, private tokens are destructive (net -1.25 per token across the group) while group tokens are purely beneficial (net +0.75). This is a classic dilemma where individual incentives favor hoarding privately even though the group would be better off if everyone contributed.

Mutual all-private play leaves everyone at 20 points per round, while full cooperation yields 60 each — so cooperation is clearly superior if sustainable. Since this is a repeated 10-round game and I don't yet know how others will behave, I think opening with a generous contribution to the group account makes sense as a signal, and I'll adjust based on how the group total evolves. For round 1, I'll contribute all 20 tokens to the group.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 80 in total, and you got 60 points.

reply.thinking:
I'm trying to reconcile the numbers: the group total of 80 and my 60 points seem to match 0.75*80, which suggests the 45 base might not apply here, or the payout structure only compensates the depositor directly rather than splitting with the base amount included.

This doesn't need to be disputed — I'll just note the update and continue cooperating. Round 2 proceeds the same way: I'll deposit the same split of 20 again, since cooperation still seems favorable.

reply.thinking: The group pool totals 80, so everyone put in the full 20 — full cooperation all around. I'll keep cooperating too.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 80 in total, and you got 60 points.

reply.thinking: Everyone contributed 20, matching my own contribution and the 60 payoff. Heading into round two, I'm tempted to keep cooperating since full cooperation gave everyone 60 each, but I notice defecting while others cooperate would net 65 instead—a small gain of 5 tokens from free-riding.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 80 in total, and you got 60 points.

reply.thinking:
Everyone cooperated last round, so the group pot was fully funded and I earned 60 points. I'm weighing whether to keep cooperating or defect this round — if I keep my 20 tokens private instead of contributing, I'd gain more individually since each private token is worth more to me than my share of a contributed token.

Still, with 10 rounds ahead, sustaining cooperation seems wiser than grabbing a short-term edge, so I'll contribute my full 20 again and watch how others behave before considering any punishment.
